text:
Sam B: Heads up — we're seeing token-streaming hiccups from the us-west-2b GPU fleet starting ~14:03 UTC. High tail latency and a cluster of 'rpc deadline exceeded' on streaming calls. :eyes:
Priya K: Can you paste the agg error lines? also which pool?
Sam B: usw2-gpu-pool-b (dedicated). Sample logs:

```
2026-03-18T14:03:12Z ERROR call=streaming.rpc id=abc123 stage=output latency_ms=1200 err="rpc deadline exceeded"
2026-03-18T14:03:13Z WARN  net: rtt spikes=160 stream_id=xyz token_delay_ms=950
```

Sam B: tcpdump shows out-of-order packets and a burst pattern: seq gaps then rapid reordering.
Alex M: microbursts or switch-level reordering. any recent topology/config change?
Sam B: Not from infra change logs. Networking team pushed a firmware update to a ToR in rack 42 around 13:50 but not sure it was rolled to that AZ.
Luca R: Can you run a short iperf3 between two affected hosts and capture ethtool stats?
Sam B: Running now. iperf3 shows jitter and occasional packet reordering flags on UDP test. ethtool -S on nic0 shows rx_packets: 1.2M rx_errors: 0 rx_nohandler: 0 rx_missed: 0 but large rx_discards at 14:02.
Priya K: Also check MTU on vtep/tun interfaces. We've had silent fragmentation when someone left MTU at 1500 while overlay expects 9000. That leads to reassembly delays = token stalls.
Sam B: Checked: one new host (gpu-12) had MTU 1500 on eth0 while all others are 9000. suspecting fragmentation + RDMA fallback causing reorder.
Alex M: That would explain it. RDMA will fallback to TCP when path MTU is wrong and cause out-of-order delivery when SR-IOV/virtualization paths mix.
ops-oncall: infra-bot alerted at 14:04: "network: packet reordering anomaly — us-west-2b"
infra-bot: alert details: detector=stream-jitter-v2 severity=medium affected_pool=usw2-gpu-pool-b sample_rate=0.02
Priya K: Quick mitigation: 1) isolate gpu-12 from the pool (drain) 2) set MTU to 9000 3) bump rx_coalesce to reduce interrupts for microbursts 4) restart rdma service if present. Can someone drain and reprovision?
Sam B: Draining gpu-12 now: `redwoodctl node drain gpu-12 --reason "network MTU mismatch"`
Luca R: I'll patch ethtool settings and apply mtu: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000` then `systemctl restart rdma` if driver loaded.
Sam B: Done. After change, short pcap shows sequence ordering restored and streaming latency back to normal. No further rpc deadline errors in 5m window.
Alex M: Nice. We should add a periodic MTU/ethtool check in node-provisioning to catch hosts with default 1500. Also audit recent firmware rollouts — confirm ToR update didn't flip jumbo frame setting.
Priya K: Filed infra ticket INFRA-7528: add MTU validation + qdisc sanity check in node bootstrap. Assign to eng-infra.
Sam B: Also adding a temporary monitor rule to stream-jitter-v2 to alert faster and include 'mtu-mismatch' tag if host reports mismatched MTU in inventory.
ops-oncall: Thanks team — marking incident mitigated, will leave monitoring until EOD. :thumbsup:
Luca R: Follow-up: found one switch port where 'jumbo' had been toggled off during firmware apply. Working with network team to pin config.
Priya K: Great. Next steps: bootstrap check, firmware audit, and a short runbook entry for RDMA fallback symptoms. I'll draft runbook PR.
Sam B: Closing notes: cause = host MTU drift + switch jumbo toggled during FW roll -> fragmentation + RDMA fallback -> packet reordering/jitter -> streaming RPC deadlines. Mitigated by draining host, resetting MTU, tuning coalescing, and switch config fix.
Alex M: Thanks everyone. Leaving the thread open for 1h for any regression signals.
ops-oncall: I'll post a short postmortem if we see recurrence."
